causal-factors.name: Seat-structure constraints and majority dynamics
causal-factors.rationale: BW has 154 seats with a 78-seat majority target (and Greens/CDU have been the dominant blocs), so AfD would need to surpass both major parties to lead in seats, which has not occurred historically. causal-factors.name: Direct-seat (Erststimme) dynamics could boost seat counts
causal-factors.rationale: The BW Landtag allocates 70 constituency seats; strong performance in first-past-the-post districts could yield more seats than a plain proportional share, potentially boosting AfD's seat total even if vote share remains around 18–21%. ([bundeswahlleiterin.de](https://www.bundeswahlleiterin.de/en/service/landtagswahlen/land-8.html?utm_source=openai))

causal-factors.name: Fragmentation and 'Other' vote share
causal-factors.rationale: Polls show a notable 'Others' share (around 8–11%), which could dilute the big two or alter seat allocations, reducing the odds of AfD becoming the largest party. ([politpro.eu](https://politpro.eu/en/baden-wuerttemberg/opinion-polls/infratest-dimap-2026-02-25/state-election?utm_source=openai))

causal-factors.name: Poll standings gap between CDU/Greens and AfD
causal-factors.rationale: Feb 2026 polls place CDU around 27%, Greens around 25%, and AfD around 19%, meaning AfD trails both leading parties and is unlikely to win the most seats.

causal-factors.name: Historical precedent in Baden-Wuerttemberg
causal-factors.rationale: In prior BW elections Greens or CDU have led the chamber (e.g., Greens 32.6% in 2021; AfD peaked around 9–21% in recent cycles but never the largest party).

causal-factors.name: Momentum in late February 2026 polls for AfD
causal-factors.rationale: Several polls show AfD gaining ground (e.g., about 18–21% vs CDU ~27–29% and Greens ~22–25%), indicating potential upside if the trend persists.

causal-factors.name: Coalition dynamics and seat math unfavorable to AfD
causal-factors.rationale: To win the most seats AfD would need to surpass both Greens and CDU in vote share; current distributions and coalition patterns in BW make a first-party majority for AfD highly unlikely.

synthesis: Current polling and historical patterns keep AfD far from the top seat total in Baden-Württemberg. While late swing factors could push the probability higher into the low single digits, a genuine breach of the leading parties’ seat totals remains unlikely, justifying a calibrated probability around 5% with a broad but plausible range.
